entities.summary:
The First Battle of Bull Run, also known as the First Manassas, was a pivotal event in the American Civil War that took place on July 21, 1861, in Fairfax County, Virginia. This battle marked the first major land conflict of the war and serves as a turning point in the early stages of the conflict. The Union forces, led by Brigadier General Irvin McDowell, clashed with the Confederate forces, led by General P.G.T. Beauregard, in a series of skirmishes and battles around the city of Manassas. The Confederate forces emerged victorious, inflicting heavy casualties on the Union army and marking a significant defeat for the North. This victory gave the Confederacy much-needed momentum and a sense of legitimacy in the early stages of the war.

The First Battle of Bull Run was a significant turning point in the American Civil War, marking the first major land conflict and setting the stage for the long and bloody conflict that would follow. The battle was fought on July 21, 1861, in Fairfax County, Virginia, between the Union forces, led by Brigadier General Irvin McDowell, and the Confederate forces, led by General P.G.T. Beauregard. The Confederate forces emerged victorious, inflicting heavy casualties on the Union army and marking a significant defeat for the North.

The legacy of the First Battle of Bull Run can be seen in the changing fortunes of the war. The Confederate victory gave the South much-needed momentum and a sense of legitimacy in the early stages of the conflict. The battle also set the stage for the long and bloody conflict that would follow, with both sides suffering heavy casualties and struggling to gain the upper hand. The First Battle of Bull Run remains a significant event in American history, marking a turning point in the early stages of the Civil War.
